# FormatSpec

Everything a placeholder asked for.

```rux
pub struct FormatSpec {
    // private fields
}
```

Copy, and cheap to pass: a spec is read, never held. Its representation is private, so a value applying a spec
reads it and cannot alter what the placeholder asked for.

## Associated functions

<h3 id="plain"><code>Plain</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Plain() -> FormatSpec
```

What a bare `{}` asks for: nothing at all.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: a spec with no width, no precision, default alignment and base ten

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Spec.rux#L84)


<h3 id="precision"><code>Precision</code></h3>

```rux

```

How many characters of text to keep, or how many digits a float carries.
Meaningful only when [`HasPrecision`](/docs/api/text/format-spec#has-precision) reports true: zero is a precision a caller can mean, so the value alone
cannot say whether one was asked for.
Borrows the spec. Cannot fail; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the requested precision, meaningful only alongside [`HasPrecision`](/docs/api/text/format-spec#has-precision)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Spec.rux#L156)

<h3 id="style"><code>Style</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Style(self: &FormatSpec) -> char8[..]
```

The style the specification named, or an empty slice when it named none.
A value compares this against the styles it understands and reports `UnsupportedRequest` for anything else.
The four single-letter integer bases are also reflected in [`Base`](/docs/api/text/format-spec#base), so an integer has no reason to read this.
The result borrows the specification text this was parsed from and must not outlive it.
Borrows the spec. Cannot fail; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the style bytes, empty when no style was written

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Spec.rux#L183)

## Related

<h3 id="padding-around"><code>PaddingAround</code></h3>

```rux
pub func PaddingAround(
    spec: FormatSpec,
    occupied: uint,
    numeric: bool,
    before: *var uint,
    after: *var uint
)
```

How many fill characters go on each side of a rendering that occupies `occupied` scalars.
Split out from [`WriteAligned`](/docs/api/text/format-spec#write-aligned) because a numeric writer needs the two counts before it starts, so that a sign, a
base prefix and the digits can go out in order without the rendered text existing anywhere as one run.
`numeric` picks the default alignment: numbers sit to the right and text to the left, which is what makes a
column of numbers line up its units and a column of names line up its first letters.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Align.rux#L23)

| `numeric`  | `bool`       | true when the value aligns like a number by default              |
| `before`   | `*var uint`  | receives the count of fill characters that precede the rendering |
| `after`    | `*var uint`  | receives the count that follow it                                |

<h3 id="write-aligned"><code>WriteAligned</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteAligned(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec,
    rendered: char8[..],
    numeric: bool
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes `rendered` into `writer` under `spec`'s width, fill and alignment.
Width is measured in Unicode scalar values rather than bytes, so a name with an accent pads the same as one
without. A rendering already at or past the requested width is written through unpadded.
Reports whatever the writer reported. A failure part-way leaves whatever the destination had already accepted;
what that means is the destination's own documented guarantee.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Align.rux#L69)

**Parameters**

| Name       | Type              | Description                                                |
| ---------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `writer`   | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                                            |
| `spec`     | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for                             |
| `rendered` | `char8[..]`       | the already-rendered text, which must be well-formed UTF-8 |
| `numeric`  | `bool`            | true when the value aligns like a number by default        |

**Returns**: success when the padded rendering was accepted in full

<h3 id="format-align"><code>FormatAlign</code></h3>

```rux
pub enum FormatAlign: int32 {
    Default = 0,
    Left = 1,
    Center = 2,
    Right = 3
}
```

Where the padding goes when the rendering is narrower than the width.
Copy, carrying no payload.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Spec.rux#L18)

**Cases**

| Name      | Value | Description                                                               |
| --------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default` | `0`   | The type's own default: numbers to the right, text to the left.           |
| `Left`    | `1`   | The value at the start, fill after it.                                    |
| `Center`  | `2`   | The value in the middle, fill on both sides, the odd column on the right. |
| `Right`   | `3`   | The value at the end, fill before it.                                     |

<h3 id="format-base"><code>FormatBase</code></h3>

```rux
pub enum FormatBase: int32 {
    Decimal = 0,
    Binary = 1,
    Octal = 2,
    LowerHex = 3,
    UpperHex = 4
}
```

The base an integer renders in.
Copy, carrying no payload. A negative signed integer renders in every base as a minus sign followed by the
digits of its magnitude, not as its two's-complement bits: `{:b}` of `-5` is `-101` and `{:#x}` of `-255` is
`-0xff`. That keeps the text of a value independent of the width of the type it happens to be stored in.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Spec.rux#L34)

**Cases**

| Name       | Value | Description                                                        |
| ---------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Decimal`  | `0`   | Base ten, the default.                                             |
| `Binary`   | `1`   | Base two, `b`, prefixed `0b` under `#`.                            |
| `Octal`    | `2`   | Base eight, `o`, prefixed `0o` under `#`.                          |
| `LowerHex` | `3`   | Base sixteen with lower-case digits, `x`, prefixed `0x` under `#`. |
| `UpperHex` | `4`   | Base sixteen with upper-case digits, `X`, prefixed `0x` under `#`. |

<h3 id="parse-format-spec"><code>ParseFormatSpec</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ParseFormatSpec(text: char8[..]) -> FormatSpec ! FormatError
```

Parses the text between `{:` and `}`.
The grammar is `[[fill]align][+][#][0][width][.precision][style]`, every piece optional, so the empty
specification is well-formed and asks for nothing. A style is an identifier: an ASCII letter followed by
letters, digits, `_` or `-`. That covers the single-letter integer bases `b`, `o`, `x` and `X`, which also set
[`Base`](/docs/api/text/format-spec#base) so an integer need not inspect the style text, the float styles `e` and `E` for scientific notation, and
the domain styles such as `iso8601` and `hyphenated` that a value interprets for itself.
Syntax is recognized here once; whether a style or flag _applies_ is the value's question, since only the value
knows whether a precision means digits, characters or nothing at all. A specification this accepts may still be
refused with `UnsupportedRequest` by the value it is handed to.
The returned specification's style borrows `text`. It must not outlive the specification text it was parsed
from, and nothing here tracks that.
Reports `InvalidSpecification` carrying the zero-based byte offset into `text` where parsing stopped: an
unprintable or brace fill, a `.` with no digits after it, a width or precision whose arithmetic will not fit a
`uint`, or any byte that can begin none of the remaining pieces. Nothing is written and no partial
specification escapes.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Spec.rux#L300)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type        | Description                                                         |
| ------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text` | `char8[..]` | the specification body, without the surrounding braces or the colon |

**Returns**: the parsed specification, or where it was malformed

<h3 id="reject-style"><code>RejectStyle</code></h3>

```rux
pub func RejectStyle(spec: FormatSpec) -> ! FormatError
```

Refuses a specification that names any style.
The parser recognizes a style wherever the grammar allows one; whether it _means_ anything is the value's
question. A value with no styles of its own calls this so that `{:q}` is refused rather than silently rendered
as though nothing had been asked for.
Reports `UnsupportedRequest` when a style was written.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Spec.rux#L383)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type         | Description                |
| ------ | ------------ | -------------------------- |
| `spec` | `FormatSpec` | the specification to check |

**Returns**: success when no style was named

<h3 id="reject-non-base-style"><code>RejectNonBaseStyle</code></h3>

```rux
pub func RejectNonBaseStyle(spec: FormatSpec) -> ! FormatError
```

Refuses a specification whose style is not one of the integer bases.
What an integer supports is exactly `b`, `o`, `x` and `X`, and each of those is already reflected in [`Base`](/docs/api/text/format-spec#base).
So a style that left the base decimal is one this value has no meaning for, which is what this refuses. It is
the integer counterpart of [`RejectStyle`](/docs/api/text/format-spec#reject-style) and exists for the same reason.
Reports `UnsupportedRequest` for a style that names no base.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Spec.rux#L396)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type         | Description                |
| ------ | ------------ | -------------------------- |
| `spec` | `FormatSpec` | the specification to check |

**Returns**: success when no style was named, or the style named a base
